_comment: Daily telemetry simulator configuration (afp_ml simulate). Data, not code: edit here, never in the module.

generation._comment: Each aircraft/metric continues as an AR(1) process around its own recent history: mean, standard deviation and lag-1 autocorrelation are estimated from the last history_days of that aircraft's readings, values are clamped to the aircraft's observed range, and each metric is missing (null) at the aircraft's observed rate. Seeded by aircraft + timestamp, so a given hour is always generated identically. No failure, maintenance or degradation event is ever injected.

status_flag_rule._comment: The source system's own per-reading flag, inferred from the supplied file: this rule reproduces all 26,707 flags in it (0 mismatches, verified 2026-10-27). It is NOT the BR-01 business threshold (35 PSI / 700 C). hot_above_c and low_pressure_at_or_below_psi are fixed exactly by the data; cold_below_c lies anywhere in (393.3, 411.0] and high_pressure_at_or_above_psi in (63.5, 71.4] - any value in those ranges reproduces the file.
status_flag_rule.critical_when: hot OR low_pressure OR cold OR high_pressure

etl._comment: The new day's records are handed to the EXISTING ingestion path (the API's raw-upload service via its CLI) as the run_as DataEngineer. Success is reported only when the resulting telemetry_import is Completed. data_source is the ETL's APP_DATA_SOURCE; every published record is verified under it.

scenario._comment: SCRIPTED OPERATIONAL SCENARIO (user decision 2026-10-28). When enabled, the simulator generates readings from these profiles instead of the AR(1) continuation: every rotation_days the next two aircraft in expected_aircraft order are at risk - the first Critical (engine temperature above the approved limit), the second HighCritical (temperature high AND oil pressure low); all others Healthy. Values are deterministic per aircraft and hour (normal noise around each profile's mean, plus a daily cycle). Every scenario reading's telemetry_id starts with id_prefix, so generated data is always identifiable. These are generated values, not observations of real aircraft.
